title: Rotating glyph tables with a recent-word tray
method: A nonlinguistic scribe uses overlapping character tables, fitted only on certain paragraph lines of the 192 public practice-training folios. Each table lists the next glyph, word space or end of line after up to four previous characters; unseen contexts fall back to shorter ones. The tables are built separately for paragraph-opening lines and other lines. To allow local drift without using manuscript labels, the scribe changes between consecutive 12-training-folio drawers every 40 output lines; for each draw the current drawer is used with probability 0.85 and the full training table otherwise. Every line starts afresh. At the beginning of a word, with probability 0.12, the scribe instead takes one of the previous 16 generated words and replaces one randomly chosen character with a glyph drawn from training frequencies. There are no semantic categories, page labels, or rules naming a measured feature. Seed 408; 1,800 lines of each kind. The sole use of the complete transcription is to reject and redraw a line containing an exact four-word manuscript sequence, as required by the copy guard. Lines with fewer than two words are also redrawn. This is an exploratory public-practice fit, not proof of meaninglessness; independently sampled pages are placed consecutively by the lines cut, so long-range results must be interpreted accordingly. Practice results: the fixed seed 408 specimen reproduces 18 of the 24 current established facts; it misses F-007, F-013, F-016, F-020, F-023 and F-027. In targeted checks, seed 409 also misses F-007 (0.145633) and F-013 (2.124060), while F-001 and F-021 pass. A no-copy control at seed 408 also misses F-007 (0.154671), passes F-013 (2.010358), and misses F-021 (-0.004653); with copying, F-021 is 0.024700. These controls use the same practice split and are not additional held-out submissions. The guard and minimum-length rule together caused 358 redraws for the submitted specimen. The line cut can make unrelated evaluation pages adjacent in the synthetic stream, so the practice F-011 result is not evidence of manuscript-scale page-distance structure.
